name: Snowflake
thesis: Snowflake — the cloud data platform, monetized almost entirely on consumption (compute credits + storage). Same core premise as MongoDB but for analytics/AI data: as AI drives an explosion in data produced, queried, and used to train and serve models, a usage-priced platform captures it directly. The bet: (1) product revenue compounds ~25%+ (total revenue grew +29% in FY26, steady at ~29% for two years), (2) NRR holds >=120% as customers ramp consumption, (3) the ~$9.8B RPO — roughly 2x annual revenue — converts; a backlog this large is precisely the market under-modeling future consumption, (4) the model stays strongly FCF-generative (FY26 FCF margin ~24%) despite a deep GAAP operating loss that is SBC-driven BY DESIGN (SBC ~34% of revenue; non-GAAP operating margin ~9% and inflecting up). AI products (Cortex, Snowpark) are the consumption accelerant — they layer new usage on top of the core warehouse. Picks-the-platform: indifferent to which AI/analytics workloads win, as long as they run on Snowflake. Competitive reality: Databricks is the scaled, well-funded direct rival (lakehouse) and the hyperscalers (BigQuery, Redshift, Fabric) bundle competing engines — Snowflake's ease-of-use + cross-cloud governance is the moat. The GAAP loss + heavy SBC dilution is the legitimate bear; the thesis requires non-GAAP margin and FCF to keep inflecting up while consumption growth holds.
key_driver: Product (consumption) revenue growth x NRR — usage-priced capture of AI-driven data growth; RPO conversion as the forward signal

tier_1_kpis.name: Product Revenue YoY Growth
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <20% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (consumption engine stalling)

tier_1_kpis.name: Net Revenue Retention Rate (NRR)
tier_1_kpis.current: ~125% (disclosed; on a gentle declining trend — backfill exact)

tier_1_kpis.name: Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: RPO declines YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (forward demand contracting)

tier_1_kpis.name: FCF Margin (GAAP)
tier_1_kpis.current: +23.9% FY26 ($1.12B FCF) — strong despite deep GAAP op loss

tier_2_kpis.name: SBC / Revenue
tier_2_kpis.current: ~34% FY26 (the reason GAAP op margin is -31%; the dilution watch, not 'losses')

nuance.bear_case: Snowflake is the most SBC-heavy name of the four (~34% of revenue) with a -31% GAAP operating margin — the equity story is entirely non-GAAP/FCF and dilution is real. Databricks is a scaled, well-funded lakehouse rival increasingly winning AI-data workloads, and hyperscaler-native engines undercut on price. If AI consumption accrues to Databricks/open lakehouse formats (Iceberg) rather than Snowflake's engine, the 2x-revenue RPO converts slower than the bulls model.
nuance.adversarial_take: 29% growth and a 2x-revenue backlog are excellent, but NRR has been drifting down for years and the consumption model cuts both ways — usage optimization by customers can decelerate revenue fast. The thesis needs product growth to hold the ~mid-20s AND non-GAAP margin to keep inflecting; one without the other isn't enough.
nuance.stress_test: If product revenue growth slips below 20% AND NRR drops below 115% in the same year, the consumption-tailwind thesis is broken — the RPO becomes a melting backlog, not a coiled spring.

thesis_breakers_qualitative: Product revenue growth decelerates below 20% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs
RPO declines YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (forward consumption contracting)
FCF margin regresses below 12% or non-GAAP operating margin stops inflecting up
AI-data workloads standardize on Databricks / open lakehouse rather than Snowflake's engine

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — outright top-line contraction.
FCF margin below 5% for 2 consecutive Qs — cash conversion broken (catastrophic floor; the per-ticker rule at 12% is the real watch).
Operating cash flow declining >10% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs.

business_model_rules.narrative: Total revenue growth below 20% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs — the consumption/'more-data' tailwind is not materializing (FY26 ran ~29%).
Product (consumption) revenue growth below 20% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs — the core engine is stalling. (UNRESOLVED until product-revenue growth is backfilled as a KPI.)
NRR below 115% — consumption ramp within existing accounts stalling. (UNRESOLVED until NRR is backfilled.)
FCF margin below 12% for 2 consecutive Qs — consumption economics regressing (FY26 ran ~24%).
Gross margin below 60% for 2 consecutive Qs — compute pricing/cost pressure (FY26 ran ~67%).
